label: Variables standardization
detail:
Have all covariates and the proximal outcome been approximately standardized so that each variable has a mean close to 0 and a standard deviation close to 1?

**Note:** once the algorithm is deployed, the proximal outcome and covariates must be standardized with the same mean and variance used in the original MRT analysis. Do not recalculate them from post-deployment data.

label: Method Determination
detail: There are two ways to set the prior for the intercept, α~0~. They differ in how much work they take and how closely the prior is tailored to your own intervention design.

label: Stop 😵
detail:
Standardize your data before setting priors.

Apply z-score standardization to each continuous **covariate** and continuous **proximal outcome**: subtract the variable's sample mean calculated from the MRT data and divide by its sample standard deviation.

Binary variables do not need to be standardized and can remain coded as 0 and 1.

Once standardization is complete, return to this page to set your priors.

label: Strength of Prior
detail:
The strength of prior determines how soon the accruing data determine which intervention option is delivered. A **smaller** Prior Standard Deviation gives more weight to prior knowledge derived from the MRT, so intervention decisions will change more cautiously. This may be appropriate when you have strong confidence in the prior knowledge. Conversely, a **larger** Prior Standard Deviation allows the algorithm to personalize intervention decisions more quickly based on each participant's data, but may make these decisions more sensitive to noise, especially early in the intervention.

If you are unsure what value to choose, a **weakly informative prior** might be a reasonable starting point. This choice of prior standard deviation is viewed as flexible enough to let the data speak for itself while providing robustness to errors when the amount of data is small.

For more detailed guidance, see the [Stan Prior Choice Recommendations](https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/wiki/prior-choice-recommendations).

label: Fit participant-specific regression models using MRT data
detail:
To obtain prior means and standard deviations, we suggest you fit person-specific regression models, one per person in the MRT data (using approximately standardized covariates and proximal outcome). If a person does not have a minimum number of decision points, you might use [ridge regression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ridge_regression). The estimators as well as their variability across the individual person-specific regression can be used to inform the prior.

For a step-by-step walkthrough, see the [code tutorial on fitting person-specific regression models](https://example.com/pjitai-prior-tutorial).

label: Set the prior from the intercept estimates of the MRT regression models
detail:
- **Prior mean:** proxied by the average of the estimated intercepts across individuals.
- **Prior variance:** proxied by the sample variance of the intercept coefficients.
